texts.facts: JUDGMENT: 1. The order impugned in this appeal is dated 30.12.2022 of Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (referred as AO) holding appellants responsible for violation on various terms and conditions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and imposing penalties on them. BRIEF FACTS 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 15.10.2018, the FSO bought a sample of "Foxnuts" from the appellants. The sample consisted 12 containers of 100 gm each, same were divided into four counterparts by pouring equally into four clean and dry glass bottles, fastened and sealed according to rules and regulations, signed by the FBO and sample was taken as required and designated officer code slip was pasted on all. One of the sample was sent to Food Analyst on 16.10.2018 and the rest counterparts were deposited in sealed packet with the designated officer. The Food Analyst submitted the report on 29.10.2018 and found the sample to be "Misbranded" as there was violation of provision of 23 (1), Section 26 (1), Section 26 (2) (ii) read with Section 3 (1) (zf) and violated Section 27(3) (c) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. M/s. Sun Organic Industries Pvt. Ltd. has also violated Section 27(1) of the FSS Act, 2003, which is punishable under Section 52 of the Act, 2006. 3. An opportunity was given to appellant to file an appeal under Section 46 (4) of the Act against the aforesaid report by the Designated Officer but no concerned person turned up for the same. 4. AO has held that appellant no. 8 has violated Section 27 (1) of the FSS Act, 2003 which is punishable under Section 52 FSS Act, 2006 and Regulation No. 2.3.24 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation's, 2011 and other appellants have violated Section 23(1), Section 26(1), Section 26(2) (ii) read with Section 3 (1) (zf) of the FSS Act, 2006. Accordingly, appellant no. 1 to 5 and 7 were levied penalty of Rs. 25,000/- each and appellant nos. 6 and 8 were levied penalty of Rs. 50,000/- each. GROUNDS OF CHALLANGE: 5. The Adjudicating Officer has passed the impugned order without application of mind. The allegation "the best before shall be written in Capital Letter" was not mentioned as minor labeling defects and cannot be put in misbranded category. It is stated that opinion of public analyst is based on complete misinterpretation of the provision of law and report of the Food Analyst lacks evidentary value and beyond Kailash Chand Pandey And Others vs Food Safety Officer Naresh Kumar Sharma on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183849052/ 2 the scope of the FSS Act, 2006. It is urged that proper procedure prescribed by law has neither been adopted by the FSO/Department nor by the Adjudicating Officer. The case of the respondent is based on Food Analyst report dated 29.10.2018. The allegations made in this report i.e. of the label best before not declared in Capital Letters are accepted by the appellants. The sole plea raised by the appellant is that this does not fall in the category of misbranding.

Counsel for appellants has relied upon two letters dated 17.07.2018 and 17.01.2020 by the Director (Regulatory Compliance) and Deputy Director (RCD) to all Commissioner of Food Safety of all States/UTs. 32. Improvement notices.-(1) If the Designated Officer has reasonable ground for believing that any food business operator has failed to comply with any regulations to which this section applies, he may, by a notice served on that food business operator (in this Act referred to as an improvement notice- (a) state the grounds for believing that the food business operator has failed to comply with the regulations; (b) specify the matters which constitute the food business operator's failure so to comply; (c) specify the measures which, in the opinion of the said Authority, the food business operator must take, in order to secure compliance; and (d) require the food business operator to take those measures, or measures which are at least equivalent to them, within a reasonable period (not being less than fourteen days) as may be specified in the notice. (2) If the food business operator fails to comply with an improvement notice, his licence may be suspended. (3) If the food business operator still fails to comply with the improvement notice, the Designated Officer may, after giving the licensee an opportunity to show cause, cancel the licence granted to him: Kailash Chand Pandey And Others vs Food Safety Officer Naresh Kumar Sharma on 28 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183849052/ 5 Provided that the Designated Officer may suspend any licence forthwith in the interest of public health for reasons to be recorded in writing. (4) Any person who is aggrieved by - (a) an improvement notice; or (b) refusal to issue a certificate as to improvement; or (c) cancellation or suspension or revocation of licence under this Act, may appeal to the Commissioner of Food Safety whose decision thereon, shall be final. (5) The period within which such an appeal may be brought shall be- (a) fifteen days from the date on which notice of the decision was served on the person desiring to appeal; or (b) in the case of an appeal under sub-section (1), the said period or the period specified in the improvement notice, whichever expires earlier.
